transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-03
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Reyes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Ethan Cole (CascadeCloud Head of Partnerships), Maya Singh (CascadeCloud Cloud Solutions Architect), Liam O'Connor (CascadeCloud CTO)

Summary: Intro & discovery for partner model, technical compat and pilot.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan with Redwood, appreciate you making time. Quick intros?
[00:12] Ethan: Hey Jordan, Ethan here, head of partnerships at CascadeCloud. Glad to connect.
[00:16] Maya: Maya, I'm the cloud solutions architect, I'll lead the technical side.
[00:19] Liam: Liam, CTO, will jump in on architecture and procurement questions.
[00:23] Priya: Hi all, Priya from Redwood, I'm the solutions engineer, I'll follow up on technical questions and pilot plans.

[00:35] Jordan: Great. Goal for today is two-fold: understand whether a partnership makes sense commercial/tech-wise, and if so, define an initial pilot scope. We're thinking about resell or co-sell models.
[00:46] Ethan: Yeah we saw your partner program doc, and from a GTM angle resell sounds interesting, but we need to make sure integration work isn't huge.

[01:05] Maya: On tech, our customers care about VPC isolation and KMS integration for keys. Can you run in our VPC or do you require traffic back to Redwood control plane?
[01:18] Priya: Good question. For Redwood Private we do a private control plane option — you can host control plane in your VPC and we offer a dedicated dataplane option as well. For dedicated pools we can also do VPC peering and private endpoints. There are a couple of flavors depending on compliance needs.
[01:35] Liam: Are there any managed KMS integrations or HSM support? We need FIPS/HSM for certain customers.
[01:40] Priya: Yes, we integrate with major KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS), and we have HSM options for Private. Might need a deeper security review for FIPS specifics.

[02:05] Ethan: From partnership side, commercial model — do you have partner discounts for committed Dedicated capacity?
[02:12] Jordan: We do committed capacity pricing — reserved GPU pools — and we have partner-specific margins for resell. I'll share the bands after the call.

[02:35] Maya: On the inference runtime: we run mixed workloads — some chat endpoints, some embeddings at scale. How do you handle batching and KV cache across multi-tenant pools?
[02:48] Priya: Our runtime supports continuous batching and KV cache. For multi-tenant pools we use per-customer KV namespaces and intelligent routing to honor latency SLOs; for Dedicated we can give you a pinned pool and more predictable performance. There might be transcription hiccups here, sorry — by KV cache i mean the key-value attention cache.

[03:10] Liam: Can you run large models with quantization? Some of our cost targets need int8 or 4-bit quantized execution.
[03:20] Priya: Yes, we support quantization-friendly execution paths, and our compiler selects kernels based on model arch and hardware. In some cases we recommend model variants that trade a small bit of quality for big cost wins. We'll include recommended quant profiles in the POC plan.

[03:45] Ethan: Security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, audit logs — do you provide tenant-level audit logs?
[03:53] Jordan: Yes SOC2; we have SSO with SAML, RBAC, and per-tenant audit logs. For Private we can preserve logs on customer side and integrate with their SIEM. We'll share SOC2 report and security brief.

[04:10] Maya: Network topology — routing, egress. If we peer, does traffic ever go over public internet? We have strict egress rules.
[04:18] Priya: For VPC peering and private endpoints, traffic remains within the peered network. For hosted API some customers prefer private network paths. We'll map options in the technical deep-dive.

[04:40] Ethan: On GTM, how do you typically handle co-marketing and leads? Do you have a partner portal?
[04:48] Jordan: We have partner enablement — sales kits, joint case studies, and a partner portal. For resell we can support lead handoff flows and joint pipeline plays.

[05:05] Liam: Performance targets — our benchmarks target 95th/99th latency under load. Can you share numbers for p99 with 2k token sequences?
[05:16] Priya: We'll need to run the benchmark—performance depends on model choice, sequence length, and GPU type. On Ampere A100 vs Hopper/T4 differences we can show ranges; but a live POC where we control hardware will be best. We'll propose config options in the plan.

[05:40] Ethan: Ok next steps?

[05:45] Jordan: Typical pilot is 4-6 weeks from agreement to end, depending on access to datasets and hardware. If we align this month we can start a Jan pilot.

[06:05] Maya: Any gotchas we should know for private deployments — service updates, control plane upgrades? We need predictable change windows.
[06:14] Priya: For Private we support customer-managed control plane and we provide clear upgrade windows; for Dedicated we have scheduled maint windows and optional extended notice for enterprise customers.

[06:35] [short cross-talk, background noise]

[06:50] Liam: On compliance paperwork — we need DPA, security questionnaire and potentially penetration test approval.
[06:58] Jordan: We'll share our DPA and an NDA if helpful, plus an RFP-friendly security packet.

[07:15] Ethan: Good, let's talk pilot scope. We want to test two use cases: embeddings at scale for semantic search, and chat generation for support workflows. For embeddings we have 100M records in prod-ish and want throughput and cost numbers. For chat we need p99 latency under 800ms for typical turns.

[07:40] Priya: For embeddings at that scale we recommend a Dedicated pool with optimized batching and caching. We'll propose binning strategies and caching configs to reduce unit costs. For chat we'll evaluate model variant plus prefix caching to hit latency SLO.

[08:05] Maya: What about telemetry and dashboarding? We need token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency graphs.

[08:13] Priya: The Redwood Console exposes token-level cost, per-route dashboards, tracing hooks and error analysis. We can enable data retention options per partner.

[08:30] Ethan: On commercial terms — if we resell, do we get a margin and lead credit?

[08:36] Jordan: Yes to both, we have partner tiers, margins scale with commit amount and co-sell activity. I'll include an example revenue share in the partner deck.

[08:52] Liam: Any particular hardware partners you prefer or have validated stacks with? Our infra partners include NovaEdge and TitanGrid.

[09:00] Priya: We run on a variety of GPU stacks; we have internal perf profiles for common providers (NVIDIA, Ampere, Hopper families) and partner programs with some hardware vendors. We'll share performance matrices — note these are approximate until we run bench.

[09:20] Ethan: Ok next steps?

[09:25] Jordan: Recap: we'll send partner one-pager and pricing bands, Priya will send benchmark plan, CascadeCloud will share network/KMS diagrams and compliance contacts. Then schedule a week-of-14-Dec technical deep-dive to line up pilot infra.

[09:40] Maya: Sounds good. One question — if we do resell, how does support work? Level 1 through us and level 2 through Redwood?

[09:48] Jordan: Typically partner handles first-line support, we provide SE escalation and an enterprise SLA for Dedicated customers. We'll document escalation playbooks.

[10:05] [brief pause]

[10:20] Ethan: Can you also include an example SOW for pilot? That would help our procurement.

[10:26] Jordan: Yes, will include a sample SOW and estimated timelines.

[10:40] Priya: I'll also include a checklist for data requirements for the embeddings workload and suggested test dataset snapshots so you can prepare.

[11:00] Liam: On billing — do you support invoicing via partner or direct billing to end customer?

[11:07] Jordan: Both models supported: partner-billed or direct depending on deal. We'll outline tradeoffs in the deck.

[11:25] Ethan: Perfect. Anything else?

[11:30] Jordan: I think that's it. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.

[11:40] Maya: Thanks.

[11:42] Liam: Thanks all.
